1.e4 e5 2.f4 exf4 3.Nf3 Nc6 4.Nc3 g5 5.d.strategy: Aims the bishop at f7 and leaves the knight en prise, ready to give it up for open lines against the king. With a pawn on d4 White also holds a strong centre and has the c1-bishop pointing at f4, which makes the sacrifice more than a bare attack.

Takes the knight, the most common reply. Black is a piece up, but the king has not castled, the g-file is open and White's queen recaptures with play against the f4 pawn and the bishop eyes f7, so Black has to consolidate quickly.
